content: 1. Fosphenytoin reduces the levels or effects of ritonavir by enhancing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Exercise caution and monitor closely when these drugs are co-administered. 2. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate exposure to R406, the active metabolite of fostamatinib. 3. Fostamatinib increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of fostamatinib may elevate concentrations of P-gp substrates, necessitating dosage reductions to avoid toxicities. 4. Garlic decreases ritonavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of gefitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may heighten the risk of gefitinib-related adverse effects. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of gentamicin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of ritonavir by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ritonavir may either increase or decrease glimepiride levels. Use alternatives if available. Reports indicate hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ritonavir may either increase or decrease glipizide levels. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors necessitate caution and monitoring. 10. Ritonavir may either increase or decrease glyburide levels. Use alternatives if available. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Grapefruit increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Griseofulvin decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ritonavir increases guanfacine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly elevate guanfacine plasma concentrations. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose to half the recommended amount when co-administered. No specific recommendations exist for immediate-release guanfacine. 14. Ritonavir increases haloperidol levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ritonavir increases hydrocodone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may elevate hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are essential. 16. Ritonavir increases hydrocortisone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Hydrocortisone decreases ritonavir levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ritonavir increases hydromorphone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Ritonavir increases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ritonavir decreases ifosfamide levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. However, ritonavir increases ifosfamide effects by inhibiting CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inducers may increase the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active metabolite. Monitor for increased effects or toxicities. 20. Ritonavir increases iloperidone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, potentially increasing plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ritonavir increases imatinib levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ritonavir increases imipramine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ritonavir increases indacaterol levels by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Indinavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin aspart due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin degludec through pharmacodynamic antagonism. HIV protease inhibitors may cause new-onset diabetes mellitus, exacerbate existing diabetes, and induce hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Ritonavir decreases the effects of insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin lispro, insulin NPH, and regular human insulin due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ritonavir decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Isoniazid increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir increases istradefylline levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Istradefylline increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Ritonavir increases itraconazole levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day in patients receiving ritonavir. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 32. Ritonavir increases ivacaftor levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce ivacaftor dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor and its M1 metabolite may inhibit P-glycoprotein, increasing systemic exposure to sensitive P-gp substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Ritonavir increases ivermectin levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ritonavir increases ixabepilone levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Ritonavir decreases ketamine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Ketoconazole increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 37. Ritonavir increases lacosamide levels through pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration may increase toxicity. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use alternatives if available. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 38. Ritonavir decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially reducing lamotrigine levels by 50%. Adjust lamotrigine dose as needed when starting, stopping, or changing ritonavir dose. Similar interactions may occur with other ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lapatinib increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Lenacapavir increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Ritonavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Letermovir increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ritonavir increases levamlodipine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Ritonavir increases levocetirizine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Levoketoconazole increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Ritonavir increases levomilnacipran levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 46. Ritonavir increases linagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism but decreases its effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Ritonavir decreases liraglutide effects due to insulin resistance associated with protease inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Ritonavir increases lofepramine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Ritonavir increases lofexidine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors may increase lofexidine plasma levels. Monitor for symptoms of orthostasis and bradycardia. Consider dose reduction. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 50. Lomitapide increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Consider reducing the dose when used concomitantly. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Ritonavir increases loperamide levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Ritonavir increases lopinavir levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Ritonavir increases loratadine levels or effects by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Loratadine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Lorcaserin increases ritonavir levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic enzymes. Use caution and monitor closely.
